content.text: – may appear 1-5d b4 onset of jaundice
▪︎present in saliva, semen, vaginal secretions; sexual & IVDU MC routes in US
▪︎~½ of US pts incarcerated or previously treated for STI; maternal transmission at delivery → ↑ likelihood chronic
▪︎onset more insidious than HAV; fever USU low-grade; may have serum-sickness-type prodrome b4 sx
▪︎acute illness resolves 2-3wks; full clinical & lab recovery ~16wks; persistent ↑ALT >6mos → chronic
: best way to assess viral replications activity
▪︎HBsAg appears 1-10wks after exposure, ↑ before sx or ALT rise; undetectable after 4-6mos in recovery
▪︎anti-HBs persists for life (long-term immunity); IgM anti-HBc shortly after HBsAg → dx acute hep B
▪︎HBeAg >3mos → ↑ likelihood chronic; HBV DNA parallels HBeAg but more sensitive (may be present w/o HBeAg in chronic)
•antiviral therapy may be indicated if persistent, severe sxs, marked jaundice, (bili >10), inflam on liver bx, ↑ ALT or (+) HB envelope Ag present
•tx can be stopped after confirmation pt has cleared HBsAg
▪︎antivirals in acute dz only if acute liver failure; encephalopathy & severe coagulopathy → severe liver failure, admit
▪︎steroids ⍉benefit; HBIG may protect or ↓ severity if given w/in 7 days of exposure
▪︎HBIG + vaccine to infants of HBsAg+ mothers w/in 12hrs of birth
▪︎most recover in 2-6mos; LFTs may stay abnl longer
CI if allergic to baker’s yeast
Response determined by PCR-RNA viral load @ 12 & 24wks after therapy
*some tx may activate HBV, so perform HBV testing b4 initiating therapy
▪︎requires HBV (helper virus) → only infects pts w/ hep B
– confirmed by immunochemical staining of liver bx for HDAg or RT; PCR assays for
has been used in mgnt of chronic HDV
Highest mortality ← fulminant hepatitis during preg
